column1:
The FOMC’s November 2017 statement is moderately upbeat on growth and employment with soft core inflation and a gradualist policy stance. The October 2017 SLOOS adds nuance that tempers this optimism on the household side: banks tightened terms on credit card and auto loans and reported weaker demand for credit card, auto, inventory and A/R financing, as well as capex and M&A-related financing, citing the economic outlook, portfolio quality, and risk tolerance. Offsetting this, competition led some easing in C&I standards and banks maintained willingness to make consumer installment loans. Net takeaway: credit supply/demand conditions are mixed-to-slightly tighter for consumers but more neutral for firms, consistent with the Fed’s decision to stay accommodative and proceed gradually. Overall tone remains moderately positive but less so than a pure reading of the FOMC statement.
